cases.name: line into gain into master
cases.proves: an audio cable replaces the downstream port node, and a Line cable becomes the hosted insert's own `input` port rather than a node reference

expected.name: line into gain into master

cases.name: stacked cables into one inlet mix
cases.proves: two cables into the same inlet sum through a `mix` node rather than the second replacing the first. A case with one cable per inlet cannot see this.

expected.name: stacked cables into one inlet mix

cases.name: bipolar CV into a param
cases.proves: an LFO into a param becomes a `range` mapped onto that param’s declared min and max, and the param it replaced is no longer published. Non-default bounds, so a wrong min or max is a different number rather than the same one.

expected.name: bipolar CV into a param

cases.name: unipolar CV into a param lifts first
cases.proves: a unipolar source (ADSR) is lifted 0..1 onto -1..1 before the range map, so 0 is the param minimum. A bipolar source skips that lift, and the two differ by two nodes.

expected.name: unipolar CV into a param lifts first

cases.name: two gains do not collide
cases.proves: every surviving param is republished as `{nodeId}_{name}` with a fresh sequential address in topological order. Two nodes of one kind is the only arrangement where a missing prefix shows up.

expected.name: two gains do not collide

cases.name: transport outlet into a param is absolute
cases.proves: a Transport outlet lands on a param in real units with no `range` around it, unlike every other CV source, and the Transport node publishes none of its own knobs

expected.name: transport outlet into a param is absolute

cases.name: transport pulse into master
cases.proves: a Transport outlet can be an output tap in its own right, mixed with the audio ones, and `pulse` lowers to a transport node rather than to a param read

expected.name: transport pulse into master

cases.name: analysis outlet into a param
cases.proves: a tuner’s `cents` outlet becomes a `pitch` node reading the analysed audio, not the audio itself, and it lands absolute the way a transport outlet does

expected.name: analysis outlet into a param

cases.name: analysis cv outlet is a scaled pitch
cases.proves: the `cv` outlet is `(midi - 69) / 12` rather than the midi number, which is three nodes where `note` is one

expected.name: analysis cv outlet is a scaled pitch

cases.name: looper pulse outlet
cases.proves: a looper `start` outlet is the same looper node with its `field` swapped, sharing the looper’s inputs, rather than a second looper. Swapping start for end must change the canonical form.

expected.name: looper pulse outlet

cases.name: keyboard makes it an instrument
cases.proves: a keyboard cable into a note jack detects the instrument role, contributes no node to the graph, and leaves the inner `note` and `gate` params in place to resolve per voice

expected.name: keyboard makes it an instrument

cases.name: polyphony is the largest inner voice count
cases.proves: an instrument’s voice count is the maximum over its materials, not the first one’s. The monophonic Tone is deliberately first in the document, so a port that takes the head of the list instead of the maximum answers 1.

expected.name: polyphony is the largest inner voice count

cases.name: an instrument of monophonic materials is one voice
cases.proves: the voice count falls out of the materials rather than out of the role. Every other instrument case here lands on 8, so a port that hardcodes 8 for instruments passes them all and fails this one.

expected.name: an instrument of monophonic materials is one voice

cases.name: sidechain is a second audio port
cases.proves: a cable into an aux audio inlet replaces that named port and not the main one, so a compressor’s sidechain does not become its input

expected.name: sidechain is a second audio port

cases.name: a fan-out is shared, not duplicated
cases.proves: one outlet feeding two nodes appears once in the flattened graph. Expanded as a tree this case is indistinguishable from two copies of the filter.

expected.name: a fan-out is shared, not duplicated

cases.name: an instrument sums its voices into the effects after them
cases.proves: everything after the oscillator runs once, on the voices' sum: the voice graph carries one send and the bus reads it through port `send0`. A port that copies the whole chain per voice has no bus at all.

expected.name: an instrument sums its voices into the effects after them

cases.name: a per-voice control keeps its module per voice
cases.proves: an envelope into a filter's cutoff makes that filter per voice, and only what comes after it is summed. A port that sums every module after the first voice source sums the filter too, and its bus reads the envelope it cannot have.

expected.name: a per-voice control keeps its module per voice

cases.name: voicing instanced keeps a module and its feeders per voice
cases.proves: `voicing: 'instanced'` on the reverb keeps it per voice and pulls the filter feeding it along, while the limiter after it is still summed. A port that ignores the flag sums the reverb; one that does not propagate it sums the filter into a per-voice reverb.

expected.name: voicing instanced keeps a module and its feeders per voice

cases.name: two voice signals become two sends, in first-use order
cases.proves: two oscillators into one reverb are two sends, and a dry cable from one of them to Master reuses its send rather than minting a third. Send order is first use, which a port that sorts or dedupes differently numbers differently.

expected.name: two voice signals become two sends, in first-use order

cases.name: a module combining two voice signals stays per voice
cases.proves: two oscillators into a multiply's two inputs keep the multiply per voice (a product of two sums multiplies every voice by every other), and the reverb after it is still summed. A port that only looks at control inputs sums the multiply.

expected.name: a module combining two voice signals stays per voice

cases.name: evaluation order is topological, not document order
cases.proves: addresses are assigned in dependency order. The nodes are deliberately listed backwards, so a port that iterates the document instead of sorting gets different addresses.

expected.name: evaluation order is topological, not document order
